FINDING_ID: F001  
SEVERITY: 0.95  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.81  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L767](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L767) sets critical-task redundancy to total `K`, but [dynamic_management.py#L756](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L756) excludes `PM` from standard task assignment when `K > 1`. In a 3-model pool, a critical task asks for 3 assignees but only 2 are admissible; a probe returned target `3`, admissible count `2`, and assignment only to `COL/PAR`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute redundancy over admissible models, or explicitly allow `PM` to participate for critical tasks; also add a hard check that fails if the requested redundancy cannot be met.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002  
SEVERITY: 0.93  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L910](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L910) force-assigns a task even when it breaches capacity, and [dynamic_management.py#L947](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L947) only warns before returning the allocation. A probe with `L=1000` and `token_demand=5000` returned `[[1]]` plus `F1: model m1 overloaded (5000 > 1000)`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Treat `F1/F3` as real hard failures in `solve()` by raising or returning an explicit infeasible status, and remove the forced over-limit fallback unless degraded mode is explicitly requested.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L1325](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1325) says equivalence requires shared `flaw_class`, but [dynamic_management.py#L1540](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1540) unions findings on similarity score alone. A probe with identical text and different classes merged into one class tagged as the first class: `1 [1, 2]`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Require class equality in the union condition, or fold `flaw_class` equality directly into the equivalence predicate and preserve class consistency when building equivalence classes.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L1765](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1765) documents the empty-history convention as “not converged unless null_expected”, but [dynamic_management.py#L1692](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1692) still returns `True` after enough empty rounds because `kappa_set`, `kappa_rate`, and `kappa_adopt` all become `1.0`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add explicit null-data handling in `kappa()`/`converged()` so an empty finding set is non-convergent unless an explicit `null_expected` flag is passed.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L2099](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2099) implements `_abstraction_dropping()`, but [dynamic_management.py#L2113](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2113) never uses it. A probe showed `stop=True` while `drop=False`, which breaks the locked “conjunctive ascending abstraction guard” design.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Wire the abstraction guard into `stop()` exactly as specified and add regression tests for both “signals exhausted but abstraction rising” and “signals exhausted and abstraction dropping” cases.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L2670](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2670) says a `PM` transport/protocol failure should abort “after retry”, but [dynamic_management.py#L2685](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2685) checks repetition against prior history only. A probe returned `RETRY, RETRY, ABORT`, so escalation happens on the third same-type failure, not the second.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Count the current failure when applying `n_fail`, for example `same_type_count + 1 >= n_fail`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L3333](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3333) processes only models present in `responses`. If a dispatched model never replies and is omitted from the dict, it gets no `EMPTY/TIMEOUT` failure, no recovery action, and no history penalty; a probe showed only the present model in `result.failures` and zero failure rate for missing models.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass the expected dispatched model set into `process_round()` and synthesize failures for missing entries before convergence and stop logic run.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L452](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L452) only creates a `COL` when `K >= 3`, but [dynamic_management.py#L553](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L553) bases reassignment on original pool size `len(self._models)`, not active pool size. A probe with active models `{PM, one other}` returned `{PM, COL}`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In `reassign()`, decide whether a `COL` exists from `len(active_models)`, not the original pool, and downgrade to `PAR` in two-model mode.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L1659](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1659) returns `1 - adoption_delta` without validation or clamping, and [dynamic_management.py#L1678](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1678) feeds it straight into `min(...)`. A probe with `adoption_delta=1.5` produced `kappa_adopt=-0.5` and `kappa=-0.5` even though the docs say both are in `[0,1]`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate or clamp `adoption_delta` into `[0,1]`, and clamp the final combined `kappa` into `[0,1]` before returning it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F010  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44  
DESCRIPTION: The real-time monitoring interface is internally inconsistent. [dynamic_management.py#L2634](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2634) emits `MALFORMED` for a format violation instead of `FORMAT_VIOLATION`, underperformance emits no event at all, and [dynamic_management.py#L2661](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2661) never emits the defined recovery events (`RETRY`, `EXCLUDE`, `ABORT`, etc.).  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit `FORMAT_VIOLATION` for format failures, add an `UNDERPERFORM` event, and emit a recovery event after `get_recovery()` selects an action.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
